Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a negative discriminant:

$$
D=(-1)^{2}-4(1)(2)=-7<0
$$

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}-3x+4}{x({x}^{2}-x+2)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}-x+2}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $x({x}^{2}-x+2),$ and we get

$$
4{x}^{2}-3x+4=A({x}^{2}-x+2)+(Bx+C)x.
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=2,B=2,$ and $C=-1.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}-3x+4}{x({x}^{2}-x+2)}=\frac{2}{x}+\frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}-x+2}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4{x}^{2}-3x+4}{x({x}^{2}-x+2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{x}+\frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}-x+2})\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}-x+2}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}-x+2.$ Then $\text{d}u=(2x-1)\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}-x+2}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}-x+2| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-x+2).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}-3x+4}{x({x}^{2}-x+2)}\,\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2x-1}{{x}^{2}-x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-x+2)+K\end{aligned}
$$
